original_test_intent: Qualify five hundred Gen1-to-Gen4 transitions on the specified GB-NV-PVP PCIe path, requiring full expected width, valid Gen4 training/equalization, and no new PCIe or platform errors on every iteration.
original_method: Verify Gen4 support across the complete path and pin Speed Change 14; baseline link and errors; for each numbered transaction establish Gen1, request Gen4, capture intermediate LTSSM/equalization and settled generation/width, record error deltas and health, and stop before another transition if any state or evidence is unacceptable; recover out of band if required.
manual_activity: Owner/FAE validates the Gen4 channel and qualification recipe; an operator isolates the SUT, watches high-rate link/platform health, and owns physical or console recovery.
required_inputs: Pinned Gen4-capable LTSSM/NVQual Speed Change 14 configuration
Gen4 capability and firmware settings for every path component
Root-port, switch, retimer, endpoint/GPU, lane, and required-width map
Gen1 entry, Gen4 request, equalization/LTSSM trajectory, settle timeout, and transient acceptance
Loop counting, error deltas, abort thresholds, final state, and recovery
safety_requirements: Dedicated approved SUT, stable power/cooling, and console recovery
Prove Gen4 path support before 500-cycle stress
Preserve baseline and complete error history
Stop on equalization/retrain failure, late or reduced-width Gen4, new AER, endpoint/GPU/host loss, reset, thermal/power anomaly, or logging gap
Do not clear, ignore, or automatically retry a fault
agent_execution_scope: Validate the owner-approved Gen4 topology, tool, and criteria
Execute only the pinned Speed Change 14 transaction
Persist complete state and error evidence before enabling the next cycle
Stop at the first ambiguous or failed result
Do not infer capability, substitute other speed-change rows, change unrelated links, recover autonomously, or issue PASS/FAIL
engineer_actions: Approve Gen4 path and equalization acceptance
Set 500-loop timing, error, abort, and final-state rules
Own link/GPU/host recovery and failure disposition
Review all transactions and decide PASS, FAIL, or BLOCKED

review_improvement: Preserves the Gen4-specific repeated transition objective while preventing lower-generation, reduced-width, end-state-only, or post-failure evidence from satisfying it.
independent_technical_reasoning: Gen4 success is not just a numeric speed field: receiver equalization and the full physical channel must converge at the intended lane width. A transient Recovery loop or width reduction may later settle to an apparently good snapshot, while corrected errors reveal marginal signal integrity. Therefore each request needs its own intermediate LTSSM/equalization trace, settled gen/width, and error delta. The next transition must remain inhibited until that record is durably accepted, because continuing would obscure the first marginal event and increase disruption risk.
